title: What the work cost, to the penny
subtitle: One real engineering program, attributed to the penny, and a cache discipline that returned four-fifths of the bill
technologies: Context engineering and persistent agent memory

stats.label: priced model calls, each tied to its task
governed state transitions along the way

lede: Most platforms report a vendor invoice. I wanted to know what the work cost: every model call priced, tied to the task that made it, rolled up by phase and by model, with the cache's contribution counted. I have that answer for one real delivery arc under my governance platform, down to about five and a half cents per governed step. In AgentOS every model call is metered against the work order and task that made it, so cost attaches to the work rather than to a month. Budgets are part of the contract: a work order carries a spend ceiling, and exhausting it stops the work.
quote: A model that remembers beats a model that recalls, and it costs less too.
evidence: Cost attribution for AI work: 11,193 priced model calls tied to the tasks that made them, 3.197 B tokens attributed across one delivery arc, about five and a half cents per governed step.
LLM cost optimisation with prompt caching: a 94.5% overall cache hit rate from stable rendered prefixes and reused grounding, returning four-fifths of the bill.
Budget enforcement for AI agents: a spend ceiling on every work order that stops the work when exhausted, with model and reasoning effort named per role as data.
Code intelligence economics: asking the code graph cost about 5,100 tokens per code question against 29,100 for manual exploration, across 536 recorded searches.
Memory for AI agents: 289,304 stored observations recalled 452,834 times instead of being rediscovered, along 36,515 governed state transitions.
author: Corey James
